Succession war between Sundara and Vira Pandya after 1310 plus Khalji raid 1311; Madurai then annexed as Delhi Sultanate province of Ma'bar (c.1323), which seceded as Madurai Sultanate c.1335. Pandya remnant at Tenkasi. 1323 date from leads, not opened sources.

Fatimid army sent from Ifriqiya under Jawhar took Fustat in 969 (external conquest). Database period merges Tulunids (868-905), Abbasid restoration (905-935) and Ikhshidids (935-969). Q4: disorder after Kafur's death 968, 960s low-Nile famine (not verified in opened sources).

notes: Medes (external) took Ashur 614 and, with Babylonian rebels under Nabopolassar (revolt 626), sacked Nineveh 612; rump at Harran to 609. Database home area wrong: core is northern Mesopotamia (Nineveh). Q4: Babylonian revolt, post-Ashurbanipal succession strife.

Kidarites expelled from Bactria (Balkh) 467 by Sasanians with Hephthalites; residual Gandhara kingdom sent embassies to 477, then displaced by Alkhon Huns (older sources say Hephthalites). Evidence largely numismatic. Q4: Hephthalite rebellion from 457.

successor: Ptolemaic Kingdom II (same dynasty, Ptolemy IV)
source1: Metropolitan Museum of Art, 'The Ptolemaic Dynasty', Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/ptol/hd_ptol.htm
notes: Ptolemaic dynasty ruled without break until 30 BCE; 217 (Raphia) is a database period split. Q4: Cyrenaica separated under Magas until reunited by Ptolemy III; domestic revolt recalled Ptolemy III c.245 (latter not verified).

successor: Ghuzz (Oghuz) Turkmen and fragmented Khorasan regimes; later Khwarazmian Empire
